content_units: For two adults, this plan keeps a   moderate pace  , avoids very early starts, and fits a combined   activities + local transport budget of about ¥45,000 total  . It prioritizes   temples, gardens, tea, traditional streets  , plus   one especially quiet evening  .
- Style:   moderate pace  , late-morning starts, low rush
- Priorities:   temples, gardens, tea, traditional streets, quiet evening
- Budget target:   ¥45,000 total   for activities and local transport
Day 1: Higashiyama Lanes, Kiyomizu-dera, and Gion at Dusk
- Morning: Start around   10:00 AM   in   Kiyomizu-dera  , then stroll downhill through   Sannenzaka   and   Ninenzaka   for classic preserved Kyoto streets.
- Afternoon: Visit   Kodai-ji   and its garden, then stop for a   matcha and wagashi tea break   near Higashiyama.
- Dinner: Eat in   Gion   or south Higashiyama; after dinner, take a slow walk around   Hanamikoji   and Shirakawa.
- Local transport: Mostly walking; short bus/taxi if needed from central Kyoto.
- Swap outdoor lane wandering for more time at   Kodai-ji  ,   Kiyomizu-dera indoor/viewing areas  , and a longer tea stop.
- Add   Kyoto National Museum   area café time if weather turns poor.
Day 2: Arashiyama Bamboo, Tenryu-ji Garden, and Riverside Tea
- Morning: Begin around   10:00-10:30 AM   at   Tenryu-ji  , then walk into the   Arashiyama bamboo grove   after the earliest crowds fade.
- Afternoon: Cross toward   Togetsukyo Bridge  , browse quiet lanes, and pause at a tea house with garden views.
- Dinner: Riverside or station-area dinner in Arashiyama before returning to central Kyoto.
- Local transport: JR or Hankyu/Randen depending on your hotel area.
- Optional Okochi Sanso Garden or similar garden stop:    ¥2,000-¥3,000
- Replace the bamboo-focused walk with   Saga Arashiyama Museum of Arts & Culture   area browsing or a longer temple/garden visit plus tea house time.
- If rain is heavy, pivot to   Nijo Castle   in central Kyoto instead of Arashiyama for easier indoor/outdoor balance.
Day 3: Philosopher’s Path, Nanzen-ji, and Quiet Adult Evening
- Morning: Start around   10:30 AM   at   Nanzen-ji  , then enjoy a gentle section of the   Philosopher’s Path   without trying to cover all of it.
- Afternoon: Visit   Eikan-do   or   Honen-in   depending on energy level, then have a more formal   tea experience   or refined café stop.
- Dinner: Choose a   quiet kaiseki, tofu, or tea-house dinner   in Okazaki or nearby—this is your   kid-free quiet evening  .
- Evening: Short, calm canal-side walk; no packed nightlife.
- Local transport: Subway + walking works well.
- Spend less time on the path and focus on   Nanzen-ji subtemples  , a seated tea experience, and nearby museums in the   Okazaki   area.
- Best foul-weather substitute:   Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art   or   National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto   plus tea.
Day 4: Northern Kyoto Calm — Daitoku-ji Area or Kyoto Imperial Park
- Morning: Sleep in a bit and head around   10:30 AM   to either   Daitoku-ji temple precincts   for Zen atmosphere or   Kyoto Imperial Palace Park   for broad garden space.
- Afternoon: Finish with a dedicated tea stop and traditional sweets, plus light shopping for tea or ceramics.
- Dinner: Early relaxed dinner near   Demachiyanagi  ,   Karasuma  , or your departure base.
- Make this your   museum and tea day  :   Kyoto International Manga Museum   is a lighter option, while   Kyoto Museum of Crafts and Design   or central galleries pair well with tea shops.
- If weather is only light rain,   Kyoto Imperial Park   still works with umbrellas because paths are wide and flexible.

Best Route Logic for Your Priorities

-   Best overall match:   This sequence starts with iconic traditional Kyoto, adds one scenic west-side day, then a calmer eastern day with your   quiet adult evening  , and finishes with a lighter final day.
-   Why it works:   It avoids stacking too many major temple climbs, limits cross-city zigzags, and keeps most starts around   10:00-10:30 AM  .
-   Best quiet evening:     Day 3   is the strongest fit—Nanzen-ji/Okazaki has a more refined, low-noise feel than busy Gion at night.
